detaileddescription.para: Performs a depth-first traversal of the type as specified by its arguments, stopping at the next leaf node (which may be a legitimate scalar type or an empty struct or array).

parameterdescription.para: List of the partial components making up the type from outermost to innermost non-empty aggregate. The element currently represented is SubTypes.back()->getTypeAtIndex(Path.back() - 1).
Set of extractvalue indices leading from the outermost type (SubTypes[0]) to the leaf node currently represented.

simplesect.para: true if a new type was found, false otherwise. Calling this function again on a finished iterator will repeatedly return false. SubTypes.back()->getTypeAtIndex(Path.back()) is either an empty aggregate or a non-aggregate

briefdescription.para: Find the first non-empty, scalar-like type in Next and setup the iterator components.

detaileddescription.para: Assuming Next is an aggregate of some kind, this function will traverse the tree from left to right (i.e. depth-first) looking for the first non-aggregate type which will play a role in function return.
For example, if Next was {[0 x i64], {{}, i32, {}}, i32} then we would setup Path as [1, 1] and SubTypes as [Next, {{}, i32, {}}] to represent the first i32 in that type.

briefdescription.para: Set the iterator data-structures to the next non-empty, non-aggregate subtype.
